 4. The defendant Md. Soleman Ali submitted a Written Statement on 3-5-1979 in Title Suit No. 480 of 1979, subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 denying the material statements made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that he is the sixteen annals owner of the property mentioned in the schedule 'A' and 'B' by purchase on the strength of a registered lease deed of perpetuity dated 4-6-1956 being No. 6096 and by a deed of purchase of Quit Rent, being No. 6097 dated 4-6-1956 on payment of proper consideration from real owners. Since the date of purchase the defendant has been owning and possessing the schedule "A" property by erecting new structures thereon and living with the members of his family and carrying on business in a portion of it on getting his name recorded in the record of rights and on payment of rent to the proper authority and his name was also duly mutated in the Dacca Municipality and he is also paying Municipal taxes, WASA and Electric bills. The plaintiff was known to the defendant for a pretty long time and he was a peon, serving at settlement office at Dhaka, used to come to the defendant in times of need for help and the defendant also helped the plaintiff in various ways and after liberation of Bangladesh the plaintiff having no accommodation for himself and his family at Dhaka, approached the defendant allowing him to live in "B" Schedule property as his licensee, which is a small portion of "A" schedule property and the defendant out of sympathy as licensee allowed the plaintiff to live in a portion of suit land. The defendant is a Non Bengali Urdu speaking person who came from India as a refugee in the year 1950, after partition of India. After liberation war of 1971 and creation of Bangladesh the defendant had to remain absent from his house for some time leaving the schedule property (house) and business establishment including machineries thereof in the care, custody and supervision of the plaintiff on whom the defendant reposed full confidence, belief and trust. After liberation and during the disturbed post -liberation period the defendant could not manage his business and other family affairs and he had to depend on the plaintiff for such management. At that relevant period the plaintiff disclosed that to manage the business establishment and to look after the schedule property he requires a Power of Attorney in his favour by the defendant and the plaintiff had been constantly pressing for the same. In that state of affairs, the defendant had no other alternative but to agree to the proposal of the plaintiff and accordingly, a Power of Attorney was being got drafted by the plaintiff and the defendant was taken to the office of the Sub-Registrar, Dhaka for such registration of the same but the Sub-Registrar refused to register the same, on the plea that no Non Bengali is permitted under the present law to authorise or register any document in favour of anybody without permission from Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka. Being failure to get Power of Attorney registered in favour of the plaintiff by the defendant the plaintiff on a subsequent date took the defendant before one Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka and he was made to swear an affidavit dated 3-2-1973 giving the plaintiff authority and power to manage the affairs of the defendant. Even after swearing the above affidavit the plaintiff made several attempts to get a Power of Attorney executed and registered in favour of the plaintiff by the defendant and the defendant was taken to the Sub-Registrar's Office but no Power of Attorney could be registered although several attempts were made by the plaintiff in this regard. Since after liberation the plaintiff has been living in the "B" Schedule property, which is a small portion of the north eastern portion of the "A" Schedule property as a licensee of the defendant. The plaintiff being a local man and the defendant being a non-local had to get his business managed and he was also required to do other family affairs of the defendant at the relevant period. Curiously enough, the defendant got a notice from the Settlement office in the 1st week of September 1977, in the absence of the plaintiff wherein the defendant found that the plaintiff had filed an objection petition for canceling the name of the defendant in respect of the "A" schedule property in the recent RS Operation and for getting his name recorded. On the date of hearing of the said Objection Petition No. 329 of 1977 the defendant was present and raised objection and produced the relevant papers and documents in support of his title in respect of the schedule property to the Settlement Officer who on perusal of the papers and documents in possession of the defendant was pleased to reject the prayer of the plaintiff and upheld the previous record stood in the name of the defendant for the schedule property. On getting the notice from settlement office the defendant got suspicious about the activities and trustworthiness of the plaintiff and later on, the defendant came to learn that the plaintiff dishonestly removed all his machineries including a printing press machine and other goods and articles of the defendant from the said holding causing a loss of huge amount of Taka to the defendant and misappropriated the said amount. Some time thereafter, the defendant got a show cause notice and adinterim injunction notice of the instant suit from the Court, and the defendant caused his appearance on 14-11-1978 in the said suit and prayed for time to file Written Statement and on reading the plaint, the defendant could firstly come to know that the plaintiff had got a fraudulent and forged sale deed registered in his name in respect of the "A" schedule property by false personification. Thereafter, the defendant obtained a certified copy of the said forged and fraudulent document on 3-4-1979 and definitely could come to learn that a forged, fraudulent, collusive and illegal document has been created in favour of the plaintiff on false personification of the defendant to grab the valuable property of the defendant beyond his knowledge and without making any payment of consideration money whatsoever. The defendant did not put signatures on the said alleged sale deed. His signatures on the alleged document have been forged by some other person. All signatures as contained in the said deed are not the signature of the defendant and the said deed is forged, fraudulent and collusive deed and the deed was created by false personification. The defendant did not execute any sale deed for a sum of Taka 7,000.00 or for any amount on or before 13-11-1973 or any other date in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the schedule property or any portion thereof. The defendant had no or has no necessity of selling his only residential scheduled property. The said false, forged, collusive and illegal document has been created by the plaintiff in collusion with the scribe and other witnesses of the said alleged deed by illegally influencing them and some other lower category staff of the Sub-Registrar's office without making payment of any consideration money whatsoever. At that time the valuation of the property was much more than Taka 7000. The defendant did not put any signatures on any papers for bringing out Income Tax and Capital Gain Tax Certificates. Any certificates produced for registration of the said forged sale deed must have been produced by the plaintiff forging the signatures of the defendant and the plaintiff must be prosecuted for the criminal acts done by him. No right, title and interest have been passed to the plaintiff on the strength of the said forged, fraudulent, illegal and void document and the plaintiff cannot seek any relief in the Court of law on the strength of the said forged, fraudulent, collusive, illegal and void document. The defendant is the lawful, rightful and absolute sixteen annas owner of the schedules properties. By creation of such a forged, fraudulent, illegal and void document the defendant's right, title and interest in the scheduled properties have not been affected in any way. The defendant informed the respectable persons in the locality about the illegal, fraudulent and collusive activities of the plaintiff and they made attempts to settle the matter amicably but failed. The defendant has filed the Title Suit No. 98 of 1979 in the 6th Court of Munsif, Dhaka against the plaintiff for cancellation of the said forged, fraudulent, collusive and illegal document and also for recovery of khas possession of the "B" schedule property as described in the schedule below after evicting the plaintiff therefrom. 

 5. The defendant Nos. 5-8 submitted a Written Statement on 14-2-1983 adopting the Written Statement submitted by the main defendant Md. Soleman and also claimed that they have purchased the suit property contending, inter alia, that Md Soleman was a Urdu-speaking man who came from India as a refugee in the year 1950, after partition of India and he was the owner and possessor of the entire suit property in his own right till his death. He could not read and write in Bengali. He always used to put his signature in English. He did not sign his name any where in any documents in Bengali. Md Soleman did not execute the alleged sale deed in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the suit holding. He had no reason or necessity to sell his only residential house—the suit holding. He had other sources of income to maintain his family. The plaintiff created the alleged sale deed fraudulently and in collusion with the scribe and other attesting witnesses without payment of consideration money whatsoever to grab the valuable property of said Md Soleman. The original owner Md Soleman did not put any signature on any papers for bringing out Income Tax and Capital Gain Tax Certificate. The plaintiff created the alleged sale deed in his favour by forging the signatures of said Md Soleman beyond his knowledge. His signatures on the alleged document have been forged by some other person. All the signatures as contained in the said deed are forged, fraudulent, void and collusive and are created by false personification. No right, title and interest have passed to the plaintiff on the strength of the said forged, fraudulent, illegal and void document, and the plaintiff cannot seek any relief in the Court of law on the strength of the said forged, fraudulent, collusive, illegal and void document. By creating of such a forged, fraudulent illegal and void document, the defendant's right, title and interest in the schedule properties have not been affected in any way. The original defendant late Md Soleman had filed the Title Suit No. 98 of 1979 in the 6th Court of Munsif, Dhaka and the said suit of transfer to the Court has been renumbered as being Title Suit No. 516 of 1981. For cancellation of the said forged, fraudulent, collusive and illegal document and also for recovery of khas possession of the "B" schedule property as described in the plaint of the said suit, after evicting the plaintiff there from. These defendants purchased the entire suit holding from the heirs and successors of late Md Soleman in the year 1982 and they have been owning and possessing the same since their date of purchase and, at present, they are the real owners and possessors of the said property 

 (c) for passing a decree declaring that the plaintiffs are the rightful owners of the properties described in the schedule’s" and to deliver khas possession of the 'B' schedule property to the plaintiff after evicting the defendant there from with all his men and materials in execution of the decree;" imp leading Emdaduddin (the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 480 of 1978 and subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 to be the sole defendant) incorporating the whole case as made out in the written statement of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992. 

 (iv) Whether the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 is entitled to get a decree for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in respect of 16 annals share in 'A' schedule land and entitled to get a recovery of khas possession in respect of 'B' schedule land to the plaint? 

 (v) Whether the kabala deed being No. 27265 dated 13-11-1973 in respect of 'A' schedule land to the plaint is forged and not binding upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 and whether the said deed is liable to be declared cancelled and whether the plaintiff is entitled to get a decree for recovery of khas possession in respect of 'B' schedule land as against the defendant of the suit? 

 17. Mr Mohammad Habibullah, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, on appearing before this Court, submitted that the defendant of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 having specifically pleaded that the Exhibit 1 was not executed by Soleman, that deed was created by false personification, and that no payment of consideration was made as against the said deed and Soleman did not execute the said deed it was the duty of the trial Court to decide specifically as to whether the said deed was executed by Soleman and any consideration was passed against the said deed. He submitted that the trial Court without giving any finding upon those vital facts decreed the suit in a slip shod manner. He further submitted that the defendant Nos. 5-8 have specifically pleaded in the Written Statement that Soleman was not conversant with the Bengali writing and could not know how to put his signature in Bengali but the deed in question was shown to have been executed in Bengali. He submitted the same to be a forged deed out and out. He further submitted that the defendant (the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992) by producing Exhibits D, K, M, Ml, O, O(1)-O(4) and also by adducing oral evidence has been able to prove the fact that Soleman used to put his signature in English, he did not put his signature ever in Bengali. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 had onus to prove due execution of Exhibit 1 by Soleman and also had onus to prove that consideration of Taka 7,000.00 was received by Solaiman as against the deed but the plaintiff has hopelessly failed to prove due execution of the said deed (Exhibit 1) and also failed to prove payment of consideration by adducing evidence either oral or documentary. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 also failed to prove that any possession was handed over in his favour on the strength of Exhibit 1. He submitted further that the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka without coming to his own finding as to execution of Exhibit 1 by Soleman and as to payment of consideration as against Exhibit 1 and as to delivery of possession as against Exhibit 1, blindly and erroneously held the Exhibit 1 to be a valid deed, only upon considering the fact, that Soleman did not make any attempt for getting compared his admitted LTI with the LTI as contained in the back of page 1 of Exhibit 1. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 has sought for recovery of khas possession in the 'B' schedule land in the plaint against Soleman alleging him to be a licensee under him. But the Courts below neither gave any finding upon the said relief nor discussion and considered any evidence in support of the said positive case of the plaintiff. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 by adducing 7 DWs and by exhibiting huge number of documents have been able to prove that Soleman did not ever put his signature in Bengali during his lifetime. He submitted that they have been able to prove that the Exhibit 1 was a forged deed out and out and have been able to prove too that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 was given accommodation as a licensee in a part of the suit homestead, in 1972 but the trial Court and as well as the appellate Court without discussing a single evidence, adduced by the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992, illegally dismissed their suit and decreed the other suit and the appellate Court, being the last Court of fact neither discussed any evidence nor gave his own finding in affirming the judgment of the trial Court. He submitted that onus heavily lay upon the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 to prove due execution of Exhibit 1. by Soleman, payment of consideration made by PW 1 and acceptance of said consideration by Soleman and handing over possession of the suit property by Soleman in favour of the PW 1 but the PW 1 having failed to do so by adducing evidence and the DW 17 by adducing oral and documentary evidence having been able to prove that the Exhibit 1 was a forged deed out and out, the judgment and decree impugned in the Rule are although concurrent is liable to be interfered by this Court in revision. He relied upon the case law upon onus of proving due execution of Exhibit 1 as reported in 1987 BLD (AD) 306. 

 29. The plaintiff in Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 filed the suit for declaration of title, confirmation of possession in schedule 'A' land and recovery of Khas possession in the 'B' Schedule land of the plaint against defendant Md Soleman alleging, inter alia, that Soleman sold the suit property to him by a Kabala deed dated 31-11-73 at a consideration of Taka 7000.00. Md Soleman by filing a written statement totally denied the said sale and denied his execution as contained in Exhibit 1. Md Soleman denied to have receipt of any consideration money as against the Exhibit 1. Md Solaiman categorically asserted the Exhibit 1 to be a forged deed and made out a case that the said Exhibit 1 was created by false personification. The defendant Nos. 5-8 being the subsequent purchasers from the heirs and legal representatives of defendant Soleman have stated categorically in their written statement that Soleman was a no Bengali and could not know how to write Bengali. Those defendants also brought a specific case that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 had created the Exhibit 1 by false personification with the help of scribe and witnesses of the deed. The plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 also established a specific and distinct case that Soleman did not execute the Exhibit 1 and did not receive any single farthing towards consideration from the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 as against the Exhibit 1. It is their case that the Exhibit 1 was created by Emdad, the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 by false personification with help of the deed writer of Exhibit 1 and also with the help of witnesses as mentioned in the deed. 

 44. In the result, both the Rules are made absolute, however, without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree dated 30-11-2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge-in-charge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 181 of 1999 (heard analogous with Title Appeal No. 182 of 1999) dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 25-2-1999 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 (heard analogous with Title Suit No. 22 of 1992) decreeing the suit is hereby set aside. The judgment and decree dated 30-11-2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge-in-charge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 182 of 1999 (heard analogous with Title Appeal No. 181 of 1999) dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 25-2-1999 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 (heard analogous with Title Suit No. 23 of 1992) dismissing the suit is also hereby set aside. Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 is hereby decreed with cost and Title Suit No. 23 of 1993 is dismissed with cost. The kabala deed alleged to have been executed by Md. Soleman on 6-11-1973 and registered on 13-11-1973 in favour of PW 1, Emdaduddin is hereby declared void and the same is cancelled. The title of plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 is hereby declared and the possession of the opposite party plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 in part of the suit land are nothing but permissive possession granted by Soleman. The plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 is entitled to get recovery of khas possession after evicting the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 23 of 1992, on execution of the decree. All further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 1 of 1999 now pending in the Court of Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka appear to be not maintainable as being infructuous one. The defendant Nos. 5-8 being a purchaser during tendency of the suit, their title will be governed according to section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act.
